sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A Portuguese ATM offered me a 13.6% mark-up on 200 euros, twice; the EU rule it seems to miss; AI as the consumer's evidence.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: 200 euros; a guaranteed rate twice; 13.6%; legal if shown; six levers; AI evidence; local currency.

sections.label: Three prices for the same 200 euros
sections.para: The whole cost is in the offer.

sections.label: What the screens said
sections.line: A rate, a total in pounds and a Union Jack, then the same question again on a second screen.

sections.label: Where the money goes
sections.line: Accept and the ATM's service keeps the margin; decline and my bank converts near the ECB rate.
sections.para: The guarantee protects against almost nothing.

sections.label: What the law says
sections.line: Regulation 2019/518 Article 3a: show the mark-up as a percentage over the ECB rate before confirming.

sections.label: Six levers on two screens
sections.line: Certainty against fear, a home anchor, loaded words, asking twice, the setting, borrowed trust.

sections.label: Why I wrote this
sections.line: Nobody can check at the machine; with an AI agent afterwards, the evidence took minutes.

sections.label: What you can do
sections.line: Choose the local currency, ask for the mark-up, and complain where it is not shown.
sections.para: In Portugal: the bank, the complaints book, Banco de Portugal.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: One withdrawal, two screens; who runs the conversion unknown; not legal advice.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: My withdrawal, the PrompTugal.news evidence pack, the ECB rates, the regulations, BEUC and studies.
